item.title: More of the men being deported now have lived in the U.S. for years
item.description: In another shift, nearly 2 in 3 of those removed since January 2025 do not have criminal records.

item.title: A super El Niño wiped out millions of people in 1877. Are we better prepared now?
item.description: The climatic phenomenon is expected to return this year, but a lot has changed since what might have been the worst environmental disaster in human history.

item.title: U.S. strikes two Iranian-flagged tankers as tensions continue amid ceasefire
item.description: The Trump administration said it was anticipating a reply from Tehran on its latest terms for ending the war. Iran said the U.S. proposal is still under review.

item.title: As Iran war hits U.S. weapons stocks, allies fear impact on Ukraine
item.description: European partners question viability of a Trump plan to arm Ukraine as weeks of war with Iran deplete U.S. supplies of critical weapons.

item.title: What to know about the hantavirus after deaths amid cruise ship outbreak
item.description: A cluster of cases aboard the ship have been linked to a type of hantavirus found in Argentina that can spread from person to person, the World Health Organization said.

item.title: E.U. puts sanctions on Israeli settlers after Hungary drops Orban’s veto
item.description: The measures will target Israeli settlers and organizations and Hamas members, the bloc’s chief diplomat said.

item.title: Gulf nations hoped to move beyond oil. The Iran war made that much harder.
item.description: The conflict is not only threatening oil revenue, but also Gulf states’ efforts to expand their economies beyond it.

item.title: Trump says ceasefire still intact after burst of violence with Iran
item.description: The president expressed optimism about reaching a deal despite the attacks. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the U.S. is expecting a response from Iran on Friday.
